en.p: As shown in the figure, two points $\mathrm{A}$, $\mathrm{B}$ with $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}=18$ lie on the line of intersection of two distinct planes $\alpha$, $\beta$. The circle $C_1$ with diameter $\mathrm{AB}$ lies in plane $\alpha$, and the ellipse $C_2$ with major axis $\mathrm{AB}$ and foci $\mathrm{F}$, $\mathrm{F'}$ lies in plane $\beta$. If $\mathrm{H}$ is the foot of the perpendicular from a point $\mathrm{P}$ on circle $C_1$ to plane $\beta$, then $\overline{\mathrm{HF'}}<\overline{\mathrm{HF}}$ and $\angle\mathrm{HFF'}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

If $\mathrm{Q}$ is the intersection point of line $\mathrm{HF}$ and ellipse $C_2$ that is closer to $\mathrm{H}$, then $\overline{\mathrm{FH}}<\overline{\mathrm{FQ}}$. The circle in plane $\beta$ centered at $\mathrm{H}$ and passing through $\mathrm{Q}$ has radius $4$ and is tangent to line $\mathrm{AB}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between the two planes $\alpha$, $\beta$, what is the value of $\cos\theta$? (Point $\mathrm{P}$ does not lie in plane $\beta$.) [4 points]
